Front: How does a JDK dynamic proxy work, and what are its limits?
Back: `Proxy.newProxyInstance(loader, new Class<?>[]{PaymentProcessor.class}, handler)` creates, at runtime, an object implementing the interface. Every call goes to `InvocationHandler.invoke(proxy, method, methodArgs)`, which can add behaviour and call the real object with `method.invoke(target, methodArgs)`. It only works through interfaces (Spring uses CGLIB subclasses for classes, so final classes/methods can't be proxied), and Object methods like toString/hashCode also reach the handler. A lambda parameter can't reuse a name already in scope, e.g. main's `args`.

Front: Spring AOP vocabulary: aspect, advice, pointcut, join point. What does @Around + proceed() do?
Back: Aspect: a class (`@Aspect @Component`) holding cross-cutting logic. Advice: the code that runs (@Before, @After, @AfterReturning, @AfterThrowing, @Around). Pointcut: where it applies, e.g. `execution(* org.jfl.service.PaymentProcessingService.process(..))`. Join point: the matched method execution. In @Around, `joinPoint.proceed()` calls the real method; forget it and the method never runs (returns null). Wrap it in try/finally to time even failing calls. Needs spring-boot-starter-aop.

Front: Why can a Spring AOP aspect or @Transactional silently not apply?
Back: Spring AOP is proxy-based: advice only runs when the call goes through the bean's proxy. A self-invocation (`this.process()` inside the same bean) calls the target directly and skips the proxy, so the aspect, @Transactional, @Cacheable or @Async are ignored. Other causes: a pointcut that doesn't match (wrong package or method name), a non-public or final method, or an object created with `new` instead of being injected. Fix by calling through another bean or restructuring the code.
